---

 Why predikit?

Most ML pipelines stop at .predict() . Getting that prediction callable by an LLM agent — with validated inputs, correct types, and a schema the model can reason about — requires glue code that's tedious to write and easy to get wrong.

predikit handles that layer for you:

 Without predikit With predikit 
 -- ------------------ --------------- 
 Schema Hand-write JSON Schema for every model Auto-generated from your Pydantic BaseModel 
 Type safety Manual casting, silent failures Pydantic v2 validation with clear error messages 
 LLM integration OpenAI / LangChain boilerplate per model .to openai() / .to langchain() in one line 
 Ensemble routing Custom aggregation logic per project ModelEnsemble with 5 built-in strategies 
 Confidence handling Write your own threshold checks confidence threshold + on low confidence 
 Model registries Manual MLflow / Snowflake registry calls from mlflow() / from snowflake() loaders 
 Async asyncio.get event loop().run in executor(...) await tool.ainvoke(inputs) 

---

 Works with

predikit is designed to plug into the tools your team already uses:

 Models — scikit-learn · XGBoost

 LLM frameworks — OpenAI function calling · LangChain · any tool-calling API that accepts JSON Schema

 Model registries — MLflow Model Registry · Snowflake Model Registry

 Validation — Pydantic v2

 Async — asyncio -compatible via ainvoke()

 Core API

 ModelTool 

 

 Method Returns What it does 
 -------- --------- -------------- 
 .invoke(input dict) dict Validates → predicts → returns {output name: value} 
 .ainvoke(input dict) dict Async version of .invoke() 
 .invoke many(input dicts) list[dict] Validates and predicts a batch in one model call 
 .ainvoke many(input dicts) list[dict] Async version of .invoke many() 
 .to openai() dict OpenAI function-calling schema 
 .to langchain() StructuredTool LangChain tool 
 .to callable() Callable Plain Python function

 ModelEnsemble 

Call multiple models and reconcile their outputs in one step:

 

 Strategy Behaviour 
 ---------- ----------- 
 "collect" Merges all outputs into one dict (tools can have different output name ) 
 "mean" Averages numeric outputs (all tools must share output name ) 
 "vote" Majority class vote (all tools must share output name ) 
 "weighted mean" Weighted average — provide a weights list 
 "weighted vote" Weighted majority vote — provide a weights list 

 ModelEnsemble exposes the same .invoke() , .ainvoke() , .invoke many() , .ainvoke many() , .to openai() , and .to langchain() interface as ModelTool .

 Input validation and coercion

Inputs are validated by the Pydantic model before an estimator runs. This produces useful errors
for missing fields and incompatible values, while common LLM scalar strings are handled before
validation: numeric strings work for int and float ; boolean fields accept true/false ,
 yes/no , 1/0 , and on/off .

For DataFrame-trained models, schema field names must match training columns exactly; predikit
uses the estimator's feature names to order values. For array-trained models, it verifies the
schema width and uses schema definition order.

 Batch and async inference

For application-side workloads, pass several input dictionaries at once. predikit validates every
record before invoking the model, makes one predict() call, and returns results in the same order:

 

Use await tool.ainvoke many(inputs) in async applications. Ensembles support the same batch
methods and preserve their configured reconciliation strategy per input.

---

 Field naming rule

 Your Pydantic schema field names must exactly match the column names the model was trained on. 

predikit maps inputs to features by name, not position. If you trained on a DataFrame with columns ["sqft", "bedrooms"] , your schema fields must be sqft and bedrooms — not sq ft , not Sqft .

 

When there's a mismatch, predikit tells you exactly which names are wrong:

 

 Tip: If you trained with a numpy array (no DataFrame), predikit has no feature names to check — it uses your schema's field definition order instead.

---

 Tool registries and exports

Use a ToolRegistry when an agent needs several models. It rejects duplicate names and exports
the same complete set of tools and ensembles to OpenAI, LangChain, or MCP. to openai() returns
OpenAI-compatible function-tool dictionaries built from Pydantic JSON Schema; to langchain() 
returns StructuredTool objects with sync and async execution; to callable() returns a normal
keyword-only Python function.

 Multi-model ensembles

 ModelEnsemble applies one input to several tools, then reconciles the results. collect merges
distinct outputs; mean and weighted mean average numeric outputs; vote and weighted vote 
select a class. Aggregate strategies require a shared output name ; collect requires unique ones.
Async ensembles run member tools concurrently, and batch methods reconcile every input row.

 Confidence-aware routing

For classifiers exposing predict proba , confidence threshold adds per-prediction handling:
 warn returns confidence and low confidence , raise emits LowConfidenceError , and
 fallback invokes a second ModelTool . Regressors and classifiers without probabilities remain
usable and warn at construction when this setting cannot apply.

intro.html:
The bridge between your ML models and LLM agents.
Wrap any trained scikit-learn or XGBoost model as an LLM-callable tool —
auto-generated JSON schemas, typed I/O, zero boilerplate. 

tool = ModelTool(model=clf, name="classify_iris", ...)
tool.to_openai()              # OpenAI function schema, ready to pass to the API
tool.invoke({"sqft": 2200})   # → {"price_usd": 370730}

install.title: Install
install.html:
pip install predikit

# Optional extras
pip install predikit[xgboost]    # XGBoost support
pip install predikit[langchain]  # LangChain StructuredTool export
pip install predikit[mlflow]     # MLflow Model Registry loader
pip install predikit[snowflake]  # Snowflake Model Registry loader
pip install predikit[cli]        # `predikit inspect` and `predikit serve`
pip install predikit[mcp,cli]    # serve a registry over MCP
